spec.title: Quarterly Business Review
spec.subtitle: A Quarter of Growth, Learning, and Building
spec.notes: Good morning. Today we reflect on what Q3 has meant for our company—not just the numbers, but the decisions that got us here and the foundation we're laying. This quarter has been about doubling down on what works while honestly confronting what doesn't. We'll cover financials, customer momentum, product delivery, and the strategic choices ahead. My goal is to give you a clear picture of where we stand and where we're going.

image.query: modern glass office building at twilight with city skyline

spec.title: Executive Summary
spec.notes: This summary captures the quarter in six key points. The revenue growth was driven by our enterprise push earlier this year, which is now paying off. We made a deliberate choice to invest heavily in product quality over feature volume, and the API redesign was the flagship example of that. The customer success bottleneck is something we caught early—we're not waiting until it's a crisis. What's not on this slide but matters: we made some hiring mistakes this quarter and learned from them quickly.

bullets.text: Revenue grew 23% QoQ, crossing $2M ARR milestone with enterprise segment leading at 34% growth
Customer base expanded to 180+ paying accounts, with 12 new logos in the mid-market segment
Product shipped 3 major releases including the API v2 redesign, reducing integration time by 40%
Team grew from 12 to 18 people, successfully onboarding in a remote-first environment
Identified operational bottlenecks in customer success workflows—Q4 priority is streamlining onboarding
Net promoter score improved from 42 to 51, with customer feedback directly informing 2 product decisions

spec.title: Q3 Financial Highlights
spec.notes: These four metrics tell the financial story of Q3. Crossing $2 million in ARR is the headline—it validates the enterprise strategy we started 18 months ago. The 23% quarter-over-quarter growth is our strongest since launch, and it's not from one big deal—it came from consistent pipeline execution across segments. Enterprise at 34% growth shows our upmarket motion is working. And 82% gross margin is healthy for B2B SaaS at our stage, giving us room to invest in growth while maintaining quality.

spec.title: Revenue Trajectory & Segment Growth
spec.takeaway: Enterprise revenue accelerated 34% this quarter, now 46% of total ARR. Mid-market grew steadily at 33%, validating our product-market fit beyond upmarket. SMB growth has plateaued—a signal we're outgrowing that segment.
spec.notes: The chart shows our three customer segments over three quarters. Enterprise grew from $420K to $775K, a $355K increase—that's where our focus on API stability and compliance features paid off. Mid-market grew from $280K to $520K, proving we have a repeatable motion at that level without enterprise-level friction. SMB flatlined this quarter at about $405K, which tells us our unit economics there are challenged and our sales motion is increasingly focused upmarket. The stacked column shows both the overall trajectory (total revenue) and which segment is driving momentum. This visual confirms what we're hearing from leadership: we've found our best customer profile, and Q4 should deepen that focus.

spec.title: Customer Retention & Expansion
spec.notes: This SWOT analysis breaks down our customer health and growth prospects. On the positive side, our enterprise focus is paying off with near-perfect renewals and a welcome shift toward annual contracts, which stabilizes revenue and deepens relationships. The weakness column shows where we're vulnerable: mid-market churn, where we haven't yet adapted our high-touch model efficiently, and stalled expansions that reveal a need for better multi-threaded sales plays. The opportunities are real—our loyalty pilot worked, and we have a clear list of upgrade candidates. The threats are competitive and macroeconomic; we can't control the latter, but we need to accelerate our roadmap to stay ahead on API features. The matrix helps us see where to double down and where to invest in fixes.

quadrants.heading: Strengths
quadrants.text: High-touch onboarding and dedicated CSMs led to 97% renewal rate for enterprise customers. Annual prepaid contracts increased from 15% to 22% of base, improving cash flow and commitment.

quadrants.heading: Weaknesses
quadrants.text: Mid-market churn rose to 8.5%, linked to slow initial value realization. Upsell conversations stalled when requiring stakeholder alignment beyond primary buyer.

quadrants.heading: Opportunities
quadrants.text: Loyalty program pilot (early renewal discount, product roadmap preview) showed 12% increase in expansion revenue among participants. 45 customers now eligible for tier upgrade based on usage.

quadrants.heading: Threats
quadrants.text: Two competitors announced similar API capabilities, potentially neutralizing a key retention driver. Macroeconomic uncertainty is causing procurement delays for net-new deals over $50K.

spec.title: Product Delivery & Milestones
spec.notes: Q3 was deliberately focused on depth over breadth. The API v2 redesign was our biggest engineering bet—it took eight weeks and three developers, but it cut integration friction significantly. SOC 2 certification in August wasn't just a checkbox; it directly won us two enterprise deals that were waiting for compliance confirmation. The customer success portal came from listening to our support team, who flagged that we were answering the same questions repeatedly. Shipping it cut support burden immediately and freed the team to focus on strategic accounts. October's analytics feature shipped early based on customer requests and is already showing promise in retention metrics. Each milestone was driven by either a concrete customer pain point or a clear bottleneck we'd identified.

steps.label: July
steps.heading: API v2 Redesign
steps.text: Reduced integration time by 40%. Enabled webhooks and real-time sync.

steps.label: August
steps.heading: Security & Compliance
steps.text: SOC 2 Type II certified. Added role-based access controls for enterprise.

steps.label: September
steps.heading: Customer Success Portal
steps.text: Self-service resource hub launched. Reduced support tickets by 18%.

steps.label: October
steps.heading: Advanced Analytics
steps.text: Usage dashboards shipped. Early adopters seeing 25% better retention.

spec.title: Operational Learnings
spec.notes: This slide reflects on concrete operational missteps we made in Q3 and what we learned. The left side names three real problems: we tried to scale our enterprise playbook wholesale and it didn't work for mid-market, we got caught flat-footed by support escalations because edge cases weren't documented, and we treated all churn the same when the root causes were different by segment. The right side isn't aspirational—each item is an action we're starting in Q4. The self-serve track for mid-market is already in design; the observability project kicks off next sprint; and CSM restructuring starts with a pilot team. This positions the company as learning from real feedback, not just executing a preset plan.

left.heading: What We Got Wrong
bullets: Enterprise model mismatch: Mid-market buyers needed faster time-to-value, not heavy hand-holding.
API support burden: Undocumented edge cases consumed 30% of engineering capacity in firefighting.
Segment-agnostic churn: Treated enterprise and mid-market churn identically despite different root causes.

right.heading: What We'll Change
bullets: Self-serve mid-market track: Launch guided templates to cut onboarding from 8 weeks to 3.
API observability project: Invest in proactive monitoring and document top 20 integration patterns.
CSM segment rotation: Named accounts for enterprise; shared pool with playbooks for mid-market.

spec.title: Strategic Roadmap for Q4
spec.notes: Q4 has four parallel bets, each tied to a revenue or retention lever we identified this quarter. The enterprise track is straightforward—we have momentum and clear deal requirements, so we're doubling down on compliance and API features that remove procurement friction. The mid-market track is our biggest operational lift; we learned that our enterprise playbook doesn't work there, so we're building a self-serve alternative. The expansion revenue track leverages the loyalty pilot that worked—we're formalizing it and systematically moving our 45 upgrade candidates through it. The competitive moat track is forward-looking; the analytics feature is both a retention tool and a differentiator against the two competitors who just announced API features. Each step has named owners and a success metric tied to the business outcome we want. This is not a wish list; it's what we're staffing and funding.

steps.heading: Enterprise Deals
steps.text: Close 3 pipeline deals; ship API compliance features.

steps.heading: Expansion Revenue
steps.text: Roll out loyalty program; activate 45 upgrade leads.

steps.heading: Competitive Moat
steps.text: Release analytics v2 and predictive insights.

spec.title: Building the Future of B2B SaaS
spec.subtitle: Q3 Reflections and the Road Ahead
spec.notes: This quarter taught us that growth isn't linear—it's built from concrete choices and hard lessons. We shipped API v2 when integration friction was killing deals, earned SOC 2 when compliance became a gatekeeper, and learned that our enterprise playbook doesn't work for mid-market, which forced us to rethink how we bring customers to value. The analytics feature we shipped early shows what happens when we listen: early adopters are already seeing 25% better retention. Q4 isn't a reset—it's a continuation of what works and a fix for what didn't. I'm proud of what this team built and excited for what's next.
